title: Leading BI work: discover, price, and get it used
course_title: Business Intelligence Basics: Designing Systems that Drive Decisions

say: Leading BI work: discover, price, and get it used.
This is the video for Module 3 of Business Intelligence Basics: leading BI work.
Discovery is where BI projects are won or lost. Talk only to the IT officer, and you design reports about data. Talk to the people who decide, and you design reports that change what they do.

panel.heading: Where BI projects are won or lost
items: Discovery with the people who decide
A clear price and a written scope
Adoption: people using it to decide
A portfolio that shows your design work

say: Then you price the work honestly and write down exactly what is included.

say: Avoid asking, what reports do you want? People will list every chart they have ever seen.

panel.heading: Ask about work, not wished-for charts
right: Which decision costs most when wrong?
When were the numbers last wrong?
How many hours does the report take?

say: Ask about their work. Which decision costs the most when it goes wrong? Tell me about the last time the numbers were late. How many hours does the report take?
Listen for numbers and stories, and write down their exact phrases.

say: Do not guess a single total. List the tasks, estimate days, multiply by your day rate, and add contingency.
For example, Kemi's tasks add up to 14 days. Her day rate of 75,000 naira is only an example to show the method.

card.title: Kemi's quote for a pharmacy chain
card.note: 75,000 is an example day rate only.

say: She adds 15% for unknown data problems, which is 157,500 naira.

say: Her quote is 1,207,500 naira, paid 40%, 40% and 20% at agreed points. The client can see exactly what they are paying for.

say: Write scope, exclusions and client assumptions into the proposal. When a new request comes, thank the person and write it down exactly.

panel.heading: Handling new requests
items: Write the request down exactly
Check it against the written scope
If new, estimate extra days and the new date
Send a short change request
Start only after written approval

say: Check it against the written scope. If it is included, schedule it.

say: Many good projects fail quietly, and managers return to their private spreadsheets. So the sponsor opens the report at the start of the meeting and asks questions from it.

panel.heading: What gets reports used
items: The leader uses it in the meeting
Retire the old reports on a set date
30-minute training per role
A champion in each branch
Easy feedback, reply in two working days

say: For example, Chidi reviews his distributor's system eight weeks after launch. 14 of 20 managers used it, which is 70%. All 6 non-users work at the depot with the weakest mobile network, so he sends them a PDF summary on WhatsApp each Monday.

cards.d: 14 of 20 opened the report weekly. All 6 non-users work at the depot with the weakest network.
From 6 person-days a month to 1. That is 60 person-days a year.
9 reorder decisions and 3 credit limit changes made using the reports.

say: Compiling used to take 6 person-days a month. Now it takes 1, saving 60 person-days a year.

say: To remember. Ask about decisions and pain. Price task by task, and write down what is out of scope.
Lead adoption by using reports in meetings, and show leaders a roadmap of now, next and later.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Ask about decisions, pain, effort and success
Price task by task, plus contingency
Write scope, exclusions and assumptions
Leaders use reports; old reports retire
Roadmap: now, next, later
